title: Retrograde access: inject the terminals, reach the cell bodies
objective: Explain retrograde viral labeling (AAV2-retro) and why it's the natural way to access organ-innervating sensory neurons.

steps.title: The anatomy problem
steps.body: A [[DRG]] sensory neuron is [[pseudounipolar]]: its cell body sits in the ganglion, but one axon branch runs all the way out to the organ (the pancreas, the colon). You can't easily inject the scattered cell bodies that happen to innervate one organ. But you CAN inject the organ — where their terminals are.

steps.title: Retrograde transport does the sorting
steps.body: A **[[retrograde]]** [[AAV]] (e.g. **AAV2-retro**) is taken up at **axon terminals** and transported **back along the axon to the cell body**, where it expresses. Inject it into the organ, and only neurons whose terminals are there get labeled. The virus uses the neuron's own transport machinery to find the right cell bodies for you.

visual.alt: AAV injected at organ nerve terminals is transported back along the axon to the DRG cell body, which then lights up.
visual.caption: Retrograde AAV: injected at the terminals, expressed in the cell body.

steps.prompt: Why is a retrograde AAV injected into the pancreas a good way to access pancreas-innervating DRG neurons?
options: It enters every cell in the body indiscriminately once injected
Taken up at pancreatic terminals, it's carried to those cell bodies
A retrograde virus can only ever work inside the brain
It removes any need to inject the virus anywhere at all
steps.explanation: Retrograde uptake selects for neurons whose terminals are at the injection site — anatomical specificity by connectivity, not just by marker.

variants.setup: You inject a retrograde AAV into the pancreas.
variants.prompt: Why does this reach pancreas-innervating DRG neurons specifically?
options: It enters every cell in the body indiscriminately once injected
Taken up at pancreatic terminals, it's carried to those cell bodies
A retrograde virus can only ever work inside the brain
It removes any need to inject the virus anywhere at all
variants.reveal: Retrograde AAV enters axon terminals in the organ and travels to the cell bodies of exactly the neurons that innervate it.

steps.title: How the colon paper used it
steps.body: The Wolfson/Ginty colon study injected a retrograde virus (AAV2-retro carrying a recombinase) to sparsely access colon-projecting DRG afferents, then traced their endings. Your pancreas plan is the same idea: retrograde access from the organ, combined with a [[Cre]] line, to get the right neurons.

steps.setup: You inject AAV2-retro-[[Flp|FlpO]] into the pancreas of a mouse that also carries a Flp-dependent [[DREADD]].
steps.prompt: Where should the DREADD end up?
options: In all the pancreatic cells located near the injection site
In the DRG (and maybe vagal) neurons with terminals in the pancreas
Only in the spinal cord, well away from the injection site
Nowhere at all, since retrograde virus expresses no payload
steps.reveal: Retrograde transport carries the FlpO back to the cell bodies of neurons innervating the pancreas; the Flp-dependent DREADD then switches on there. Layering a Cre line on top (intersection) can further restrict it to the sensory subtype you want.

variants.prompt: After a retrograde DREADD AAV in the pancreas, where should the DREADD end up?
options: In all the pancreatic cells located near the injection site
In the DRG (and maybe vagal) neurons with terminals in the pancreas
Only in the spinal cord, well away from the injection site
Nowhere at all, since retrograde virus expresses no payload
variants.explanation: Retrograde uptake carries the payload to the sensory cell bodies whose terminals were in the injected pancreas.
